differences.title: 1. ROUTING MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Defines routes by folder structure, enabling nested layouts and cleaner organization for complex applications.
differences.rightDesc: Defines routes by file and folder names in the `pages` directory, simpler for basic structures.

differences.title: 2. LAYOUTS
differences.leftDesc: Supports deeply nested layouts that persist across route changes, enhancing UX and reducing re-renders.
differences.rightDesc: Layouts often require wrapper components or higher-order components for similar effects.

differences.title: 3. DATA FETCHING
differences.leftDesc: Enables direct server-side mutations and data fetching within components, streamlining mutations.
differences.rightDesc: Requires separate API routes for data fetching and mutations, a more traditional separation.

differences.title: 4. RENDERING STRATEGY
differences.leftDesc: Components render on the server by default, improving initial load performance and SEO.
differences.rightDesc: Pages often render on the client after initial HTML, requiring hydration.

differences.title: 5. CODE ORGANIZATION
differences.leftDesc: Allows placing route-specific logic (fetching, components) within the same route directory.
differences.rightDesc: Typically separates page logic, API logic, and component logic into distinct files/folders.

differences.title: 6. LOADING UI
differences.leftDesc: Simplified creation of loading states with the `loading.js` convention for seamless transitions.
differences.rightDesc: Loading states typically managed manually with conditional rendering or state management.

differences.title: 7. EXTENSIBILITY
differences.leftDesc: Offers route groups for organizing routes without affecting URL paths, enhancing large app structure.
differences.rightDesc: Relies on strict file naming conventions within the `pages` directory.
